pitfalls.actually_needed: npm install -g @permission-protocol/mcp-guard so mcp-guard is on PATH (~/.local/bin)
mcp-guard keys init before first run; guard refuses to start with SIGNING_KEY_MISSING
use mode: observe (or --mode observe) so blocked/held tools still forward and probe reports tools/call: ok; in enforce blocked returns -32001 and held returns -32002

config_and_keys.quote: signing: required            # required (default) | off: unsigned records that no gate accepts

evidence.quote: MCP middleware that blocks dangerous AI agent actions using a simple YAML config
Your agent can no longer delete user data.
Use `observe` mode to audit what *would* be blocked before turning enforcement on.
| API gateway | MCP operates at the tool-call layer, not HTTP. MCP Guard understands tool names and MCP's JSON-RPC protocol. |
| RBAC / IAM | Those gate *users*. MCP Guard gates *agent actions* — the agent is already authenticated, the question is what it's allowed to *do*. |
→ **Blocks** unsafe tool calls before they execute
→ **Signs** every decision as an Ed25519 receipt in the Permission Protocol receipt standard, naming who or what decided
**Observe mode** — audit what would be blocked before enforcing
